headline: Profitability improves and full-year outlook raised
summary_short: Dollar Tree grew revenue 7.2% y/y to $4.98B on 3.5% comparable sales growth, expanded operating margin 120bps, and lifted diluted EPS to $1.76 (+9.3% y/y), while raising full-year adjusted EPS guidance to $6.70-$7.10.
summary_long: Revenue rose 7.2% y/y to $4.98B (comp sales +3.5%, driven by a 4.5% rise in average ticket partly offset by a 1.0% traffic decline); q/q revenue fell 8.7% off a seasonally stronger prior quarter. Gross margin expanded 120bps on higher mark-on, lower freight and lower shrink, partly offset by tariffs and markdowns; SG&A rate rose 50bps on marketing, liability and depreciation costs. Operating income was $473.3M (+23.2% y/y) and diluted EPS $1.76 (+9.3% y/y). The company repurchased $595M of stock, ended the quarter with $1.0B cash and no revolver borrowings, and raised full-year adjusted EPS guidance to $6.70-$7.10.

drivers.explanation: Comparable sales rose 3.5% on a 4.5% increase in average ticket, partially offset by a 1.0% decline in customer traffic.
Margin gained about 120bps from higher mark-on, lower freight costs and lower shrink, partly offset by higher tariff costs and higher markdowns.
SG&A rate rose 50bps on higher marketing, general liability and depreciation costs, partially offset by lower payroll costs, leaving operating margin up 120bps overall.
Management raised FY2026 adjusted EPS guidance to $6.70-$7.10, citing continued strategic-plan progress, store growth and cost discipline.
